Port input output, early mapping, PCI configuration and memory reservation mechanisms are not visible beyond call sites.
Numeric values for page size, address shifts, table counts and fixed mapping bases are not visible.
Video, debug port, hypervisor and cross debug console implementations are not visible.

findings.text: The default early serial baud rate is 9600. This value applies when no rate is given and when a supplied rate is zero or unparsable.
The two legacy serial bases for index zero and index one are hex 3F8 and 2F8. An out of range index or a failed parse selects index zero.
Conversion from baud to divisor divides 115200 by the baud value.
The real mode size word is read at hex 413. Candidate start values below hex 20000 or above hex 9F000 are replaced by hex 9F000. Reservation extends up to one megabyte.
Presence test maps four bytes at hex FFFD9 and looks for the four letter name of the bus.

Each per processor fixup stack occupies sixty four bytes. The count per page is the page size divided by sixty four. Page space and processor capacity derive from address shift widths. Table length rounds the configured processor count up to whole pages.

Clone counts spread one logical mapping across many table entries using sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six as the span. Table entries use kernel table protections without write permission plus no execute. Stack page allocation uses kernel memory cleared to zero.
Large vector usage is tracked when the saved header includes the high portion or the high register portion of vector state. In that case a timestamp is refreshed from the kernel tick counter.
Two early floating point test values are 4195835.0 and 3145727.0.
The early serial console instance is named earlyser. It points at the serial write routine. It carries the print buffer flag. Its index uses negative one to mean not yet registered.

Each processor keeps a fixup stack address and a writable alias address. A global table holds one page pointer per group of processors. Two unsigned integers hold page and slot randomization offsets. A mutex serializes first time setup.

Kernel and user configuration blocks plus a guest default block and an initial saved state become read only after boot. One per processor pointer tracks the owner of live registers. One per processor flag gates kernel use. One per processor integer holds extended disable state. A static key records whether state size is dynamic.

Boot option parsing for early output runs once during initialization. It ignores a null string and ignores a second call after a console is already chosen. It detects a keep marker to decide lifetime. Video selection applies only when firmware reports VGA mode and copies geometry and cursor row before registering the chosen console.

Low memory reservation for firmware runs once at boot. It consults a platform flag to skip paravirtual guests. Otherwise it derives a start address from firmware data and reserves the range up to one megabyte.

Fixup table installation runs on the boot processor and on each application processor. The boot path installs the top level entry at the fixed base and randomizes layout before handling processor zero. The per processor path is safe to call repeatedly.
Bus detection runs once at boot. It quickly accepts absence on certain virtual or confidential guests. Otherwise it checks a fixed signature and records presence in a global flag.
A global routine restores hardware registers from a saved software state for a requested feature mask. Callers provide the saved block and the mask of components to bring back.
A global routine saves live hardware registers into the current software state. It chooses the widest available mechanism and refreshes large vector timing when relevant.
A global query reports whether floating point use is permitted in the current interrupt context. It returns false for unsafe nesting and true for safe task and interrupt states.

Character output polls for transmitter readiness with a bounded spin and processor relaxation. It then emits the byte unconditionally. The result signals success when readiness was seen and failure on timeout.

Hardware setup selects eight data bits with no parity and one stop bit. It disables interrupts and FIFOs. It asserts modem handshake outputs. It then programs the baud divisor through the latch mechanism and restores the original line mode without the latch bit.

Port option parsing tolerates a leading comma. A hexadecimal port number selects a direct base. Otherwise a decimal index after an optional ttyS prefix selects one of two legacy bases with fallback to the first. A trailing rate selects baud with fallback to default on missing, zero or invalid input.

Memory mapped setup requires a hexadecimal base after an optional comma. It maps a single page and switches accessors to thirty two bit memory operations that index cells by register offset. A trailing nocfg marker requests no hardware programming. Otherwise baud is parsed with default fallback and a zero rate skips programming.

PCI setup parses bus, slot and function as hexadecimal numbers separated by colon and dot. It reads command, class and base registers. It rejects non UART classes unless a force prefix was given. It distinguishes port versus memory bars, enables the matching command bit, maps memory bars through early mapping, honors a nocfg marker, and otherwise parses baud with default fallback before programming hardware.

Registration refuses a console whose index is already assigned and reports a critical error. Otherwise it publishes the console globally, clears or sets the boot lifetime flag according to the keep request, and registers with the core console layer.

Reservation is skipped when the platform disables legacy handling. The size word is converted from kilobytes to bytes. Implausible results are clamped to the top of conventional memory. A sane extended data area start below the firmware start lowers the reservation start. The final range up to one megabyte is reserved.

Per processor addresses combine a page number and slot number with global random offsets. Page selection xors with one offset. Slot selection adds the other offset modulo per page capacity. The linear result is then folded to preserve low sixteen bits while spreading higher bits, plus a fixed base.
Both boot and per processor paths do nothing on systems with full stack restore. The per processor path also returns immediately when its address is already recorded, making repeated calls safe.

Validity requires both that the current processor owner pointer matches the given context and that the recorded processor matches. Clearing the owner runs on the local processor. Marking a context invalid sets its processor to negative one. Activation and deactivation update the owner and emit tracing.

User register restore runs for the current task on its processor. It warns and exits for kernel threads and worker threads. When state is invalid it restores all pending components except protection keys which are already correct. Extended disable handling is deferred to deeper restore. It then activates ownership, records the processor, and always clears the pending load flag.

Restore first clears stale x87 state on affected processors. With save extensions it synchronizes extended disable state before restoring, intersects the request with the kernel maximum, and executes the restore. The sixty four bit mask is split into low and high halves for the hardware operation. Without extensions it uses either the extended register restore or the legacy restore based on capability. Two helpers report save extension and register extension availability. When dynamic sizing is off, synchronization and validation are no operations.

Save prefers the extended save instruction when available and updates large vector timing. Otherwise it prefers the extended register save. As a last resort it uses the legacy save which clears hardware, followed by a reload to preserve live state.

The query warns and denies use in non maskable interrupts. It denies use when kernel use is disallowed, covering uninitialized and nested cases. Outside hard interrupts it allows use. Inside hard interrupts it allows use only when soft interrupts are enabled, judged by a zero soft count.

Low level restores run through a wrapper that attaches a fixup entry typed for floating point restore. The extended restore selects thirty two or sixty four bit form by build mode. The legacy restore and the extended state restore use the same protected pattern with alternative selection for save variants.
One header defines an include guard macro to prevent double inclusion. One core unit defines a marker that instantiates trace points.

A dedicated mutex protects first time page table and stack page creation. Callers check publication with a one time read before locking and recheck after acquiring. Publication uses a one time write before releasing, so concurrent processors share the same page.

Scanning walks the option string one character at a time and tests each position for known words. Recognized words include keep for lifetime, serial for port access, mmio32 for memory mapped, ttyS for indexed ports, pciserial for PCI, vga for text video, dbgp for debug port, xen for hypervisor and xdbc for cross debug. Each match runs its initializer and registers the matching console. After legacy serial a trailing indexed marker is skipped.

Table creation proceeds from upper to lower levels only when entries are absent. It allocates a zeroed page for a missing upper entry, installs it with restricted protections across clones, then repeats for the middle level. It then allocates the stack page, installs read only mappings across strides, publishes the page, and finally records per processor addresses.

A context starts invalid, becomes valid after restore plus activation and processor recording, remains valid until explicit deactivation or invalidation, and clears its pending flag on every restore path.

Polling failure is still followed by a write, so callers cannot assume suppression on timeout. Newline expansion emits two characters and can double output length. PCI memory mapping assumes the base lies in low thirty two bit space. Kexec recording applies only to specific build and transport combinations.

Firmware size is read through a direct mapping of low memory without validation beyond range clamping. Extended area handling trusts firmware values within bounds. Bus probing maps a fixed physical window and dereferences it, relying on mapping success.

Use in non maskable context triggers a warning and is denied. Affected processors need explicit clearing to avoid leaking stale x87 pointers. Legacy save clears hardware and must be followed by reload. Faults during restore rely on exception fixups rather than explicit error returns.
